why_agency_mcp_strengthens_our_moat.reason: 1. The 58-Silo Cross-Join Moat (1 Call vs. 18 Balkanized Calls)
why_agency_mcp_strengthens_our_moat.detail: Even if KCDC, GWRC, and LINZ each launch an MCP server in 2027, an external AI agent cannot execute a single spatial + hydraulic + geotechnical + title-covenant filter across 18 separate government MCP servers without blowing its token budget and waiting 25+ seconds. TopoNZ pre-joins all 58 domains onto one atomic `parcel_id` in <1.5 ms.

Government agencies serve raw 50GB LiDAR ZIPs or static 2D polygons. They will never pre-compute 7-threshold balanced cut/fill curves (`SIM-02`), 3D neighbour window shadow hours (`SIM-05`), multi-main sewer gradients (`SIM-06`), or historical 1942 stereo fill diffs (`SIM-10`) per plot.

Because of legal liability, a council MCP server can only quote the written District Plan (`D11`). It can never expose Officer Waiver Actuarial Curves (`D12/D16`), Predictive Subsurface Failure Warnings (`SIM-10 + D52 + D58`), or Private Coasean Neighbour Easement Swaps (`D03 + D07 + D27`).

Whenever an agency upgrades from messy PDFs/WFS to a clean OGC API, STAC catalog, or MCP server, our Watchtower auto-assimilates their endpoint—dropping our scraping maintenance to zero while feeding our 58-domain join engine.
